title: UGC Commerce Video Variant Plan Schema
description: Schema for structured creative variation planning in a short-form ecommerce video workflow.

task_type.description: Fixed task type for this schema.

summary.description: Top-level summary of the testing goal and variation strategy.

testing_goal.description: Main business or creative question the variants are designed to test.

target_audience.description: Audience segment the variants are built for.

main_promise.description: Core product promise that stays central across variants.

recommended_runtime_seconds.description: Recommended runtime target shared across variants where relevant.

shared_core.description: Elements that remain consistent across all creative variants.

fixed_product_truths.description: Product realities or benefits that should remain unchanged.

fixed_brand_or_tone_rules.description: Brand or voice constraints that should remain stable.

fixed_proof_requirements.description: Proof elements that must appear in all or most variants.

fixed_cta_goal.description: Desired viewer action shared across variants.

consistency_note.description: Why these shared elements should remain stable for testing fairness.

test_axes.description: Dimensions of creative variation being tested.

axis_name.description: Name of the variation axis such as hook, proof order, tone, creator style, CTA, or pacing.

axis_purpose.description: What this variation dimension is intended to reveal.

test_hypothesis.description: Prediction about what changing this dimension may improve.

risk_note.description: What tradeoff or ambiguity this test axis might create.

variant_name.description: Short internal name for the variant.

variant_role.description: What this variant is testing relative to the others.

hook_difference.description: How the opening differs from the control or other variants.

message_hierarchy_difference.description: How benefit emphasis or sequence changes.

proof_difference.description: How the proof method or proof timing differs.

objection_difference.description: How objection handling differs, if applicable.

cta_difference.description: How the CTA differs from other variants.

tone_difference.description: How tone, delivery, or creator energy differs.

visual_difference.description: How the visual execution or scene structure differs.

predicted_strength.description: Best reason this variant might outperform.

risk_note.description: Likely downside or failure risk of this version.

test_hypothesis.description: What performance difference this variant is expected to reveal.

control_definition.description: Reference or baseline version used for comparison when applicable.

control_exists.description: Whether there is a baseline or control variant.

control_name.description: Name of the baseline or control version.

primary_metric_focus.description: Main performance signal the variants are trying to influence.

secondary_metric_focus.description: Supporting metrics or behaviors to observe.

comparison_notes.description: How variants should be compared fairly.

fair_test_constraints.description: Conditions that should remain stable during testing.

asset_or_output_plan.description: What each variant should eventually become in downstream production.

shared_asset_requirements.description: Assets needed for all variants, such as product shots, demo clips, or creator footage.

variant_specific_requirements.description: Assets or execution needs that differ by variant.

recommended_test_order.description: Suggested order for evaluating or producing the variants.

reason.description: Why this variant should be tested at this stage.

decision_guidance.description: Rules for deciding what to do after testing or review.

what_winning_might_mean.description: Interpretation cues for what a stronger-performing variant may indicate.

follow_up_actions.description: What to do after learning from the test, such as combining winning elements or refining proof.

assumptions.description: Assumptions made due to incomplete information.

warnings.description: Potential interpretation risks, proof limitations, or testing caveats.

next_steps.description: Recommended next workflow steps such as script writing, storyboard conversion, or prompt generation.
